## Blocks the extraction

**B1 — `api/rendering.py:8` reaches into `tax.rules.regional.eu.vat_bands` (crime_00006).**
This is the only crimes finding that is genuinely load-bearing here. Today it's an untidy intra-repo reach. The moment `tax` is separately installable and separately versioned, that import path *becomes* the published API contract — you will not be able to move, rename, or restructure anything under `tax/rules/` without a breaking release of the new package. Fix it before the split, not after, because after the split it's a compatibility promise you've already made.

**B2 — there is no packaging metadata (not a crimes finding).**
`pyproject.toml` is a bare `[project]` stanza: no `[build-system]`, no package discovery. Neither the service nor the extracted package is currently buildable. Crimes doesn't look at this; it's still a hard prerequisite.

**B3 — the cycle blocks *verification*, not the boundary (crime_00004).**
It doesn't touch `tax/`, so it doesn't constrain where the boundary goes. But since the app can't be imported at all right now, you cannot run an end-to-end check that the service still works after the move. You'd be doing an unverifiable refactor. Fix it first so "before" and "after" both run.

It becomes a real boundary blocker in one scenario: if you widen the extraction to pull `format_money` into the tax package because it's money-shaped. That drags one end of the cycle across the boundary and converts an internal mess into a package-to-package cycle, which Python cannot resolve at all. Don't do that — keep `format_money` in the app.

**B4 — no test guards `apply_vat` (not a crimes finding).**
There are no test files in the repo. The uniform `test_gap: 0.5` on every finding is a default, not a measurement — don't read it as "half covered." `apply_vat` is nine lines and trivially testable; write the characterization test before you move it, so the move is provably behavior-preserving.
